title: 1999 HMMT February Algebra Problem 1
statement: If \(a @ b=\frac{a^{3}-b^{3}}{a-b}\), for how many real values of \(a\) does \(a @ 1=0\) ?

solutions.text: If \(\frac{a^{3}-1}{a-1}=0\), then \(a^{3}-1=0\), or \((a-1)\left(a^{2}+a+1\right)=0\). Thus \(a=1\), which is an extraneous solution since that makes the denominator of the original expression 0 , or \(a\) is a root of \(a^{2}+a+1\). But this quadratic has no real roots, in particular its roots are \(\frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{-3}}{2}\). Therefore there are no such real values of \(a\), so the answer is \(\mathbf{0}\).
